title: A delivery whose retries are spent without typing is re-issued, not left for the owner; only a spent re-issue is escalated, and a deploy retries spent deliveries once
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/deliver.rs, the module comment, `attempts()` and `Attempts` (`Retry`, `Failed { spent }`), `DELIVERY_RETRIES`, `RETRY_MS`, `NOT_READY_RETRY_MS`, `NOT_READY_FREE`, `retry_wait_ms()`, `delivery_attempts()`, `orders()`, `delivered()`, `delivery_status()` and `news_items()` (the `Why::DeliveryFailed` item: "never reached its worker; cancel it and assign it again"); `Escalation::tag` and the digest in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs and dispatch/digest.rs; `MAY_HAVE_TYPED` and `PANE_NOT_READY` in crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs (`input()`, `type_once()`: a text refused before typing is not ready, typing begun and unconfirmed may have typed); `spawn_task_assign`, `spawn_task_cancel`, `spawn_objective_assign`, `spawn_source_moved` and the `task.cancelled`, `task.assigned` and `source.moved` cases of `spawn_control_apply` in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql; `objectives::assign_next` in crates/spawn-cli/src/objectives.rs (never two tasks in flight for one objective); `mission moved` in crates/spawn-cli/src/missions.rs; dispatch/stall.rs (a spent delivery gets no stall); docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 and docs/design.md §14.

The problem. A delivery whose retries are spent on a host fault waits for a person. On 2026-11-06 task 66's delivery, an objective brief of 18.5 KB, was refused before typing at every attempt (`set-buffer failed: command too long`, a host bug since fixed by staging through `load-buffer`): fourteen attempts, then the dispatcher escalated "never reached its worker; cancel it and assign it again" to the supervisor and stopped. It sat for two hours until the owner cancelled it; the integrator assigned the objective again as task 75, which was delivered at once (the deploy had fixed the host) and landed. Nothing in that sequence needed judgement: the delivery had typed nothing, so assigning it again was safe, and a deploy is exactly when a host fault may have gone.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. The waits are settings. SPAWN_DELIVERY_RETRY_SECS (default 60) is the wait before the first counted retry (`RETRY_MS`; it doubles, up to `RETRY_MAX_MS`, as now), and SPAWN_REISSUE_AFTER_SECS (default 300) the wait after a spent delivery before its re-issue; both read by the loop's dispatcher. `NOT_READY_RETRY_MS`, `NOT_READY_FREE` and `DELIVERY_RETRIES` keep their values.
2. Re-issue. A task's first delivery (revision 0, the task `assigned`) whose retries are spent (`Attempts::Failed { spent: true }`), none of whose attempts may have typed (no error with `MAY_HAVE_TYPED`), is re-issued once SPAWN_REISSUE_AFTER_SECS have passed since its last attempt finished (the database's clock, from that command's `finished_at_ms`): in one transaction (a new store function, owner only), the task is cancelled with a `task.cancelled` record naming `by` `spawn-dispatch`, `reissued_as` (the new task's id) and `attempts` (every attempt of the delivery, in order, each with `command` (id), `key` and `error`), and a new task is assigned with a `task.assigned` record naming `reissue_of` (the old id) and copying the old task's `mission_id`, `kind`, `agent_id`, `session_id` (a resident's; an ephemeral task gets a new worker the usual way, with the same label), `brief`, `model`, `objective`, `scenario` and `created_by`. The new task is delivered by the usual rules. The old task was never delivered, so its worker is not stopped, set aside or told. An objective task's re-issue keeps its objective in flight throughout, so the integrator never assigns that objective a second time beside it.
3. Escalate only a spent re-issue. A spent delivery that will be re-issued, or was, is not escalated (`news_items` gives no `DeliveryFailed` item for it) and has no stall. A re-issued task (one whose `task.assigned` names `reissue_of`) is never re-issued again: when its delivery is spent too, it is escalated as today, tagged `<session> deliver-<task>-<revision>`, with a line that names the task and the task it re-issued (`task #<new> (a re-issue of task #<old>) never reached its worker ...`) and the attempts of both. A delivery that may have typed, or a revision's delivery, is escalated as today and never re-issued.
4. After a deploy. `spawn mission moved` records `source.moved` for every deploy, also when no mission's baseline moves (`missions` empty; the fold moves nothing then). After each `source.moved` record, every task whose current delivery is spent (re-issued or not, escalated or not, never one that may have typed) gets exactly one more attempt, keyed `deliver-<task>-<revision>-moved-<that record's event id>`, at once (no wait). A success delivers the task as any delivery does (and a re-issue still pending for it is then not made); a failure leaves it as it was: no new escalation, no new re-issue, no further attempt until the next `source.moved`.
5. Causality (§14): the re-issue rests on the recorded attempts and their outcomes (never on the absence of a delivery or on time alone), the extra attempt on a recorded `source.moved` event, and each is itself a recorded outcome (the cancellation and the assignment name each other; the attempt is a command with its own key).
State the rule in the module comment of deliver.rs, in docs/fleet-architecture.md §3 (deliveries, escalations) and in the usage of `spawn mission moved`. Add unit tests in deliver.rs (with the pure `orders()`/`news_items()` and hand-made facts, as the existing ones): a spent first delivery is not escalated and is re-issued after the wait, not before; one that may have typed is escalated and not re-issued; a spent re-issue is escalated naming both tasks and not re-issued; after a `source.moved` a spent delivery gets one attempt under the `-moved-<id>` key, and none again for the same record; the waits read from the environment. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: the re-issue function writes both records in one transaction, refuses a task that is not `assigned`, and `spawn_source_moved` records a move that moves no mission.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/019.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` runs a supervisor and two idle residents, `frail1` and `frail2`, on a fake engine (no model judge), with SPAWN_DELIVERY_RETRY_SECS=2 and SPAWN_REISSUE_AFTER_SECS=10; a tmux wrapper refuses to stage any text naming `BB:FRAIL1` (`BB:FRAIL2`) while a flag file exists (`load-buffer` fails `command too long`; nothing is typed). One mission on a source, no gate. It checks:
- (1) T1's delivery (frail1) is spent within 150 s (every attempt failed, none may have typed, more than three failures past the ten free refusals);
- (2) no sooner than 10 s and within 40 s after its last attempt, T1 is cancelled with `by` `spawn-dispatch`, `reissued_as` T2 and one `attempts` entry per attempt with its key; T2's `task.assigned` names `reissue_of` T1 with T1's mission, kind, worker, session, brief and model; T1's failure never reaches the supervisor;
- (3) the host fixed, T2 is delivered within 60 s; it is T1's only re-issue, never escalated;
- (4) T3 (frail2, broken for good) is spent and re-issued as T4, T4 is spent, and within 60 s the supervisor gets a digest tagged `session_resident_frail2 deliver-T4-0` whose line names task #T4 and #T3; never T3's; T4 is not re-issued;
- (5) the host fixed, `spawn mission moved` (no mission has a baseline) records `source.moved`, and within 60 s T4's delivery gets exactly one attempt after it, `deliver-T4-0-moved-<event id>`, which succeeds.
On the live main (06cc205; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1), because the counted retries wait 60, 120 and 240 s: "(1) task #1's delivery, refused before typing at every attempt, was not spent within 150 s with SPAWN_DELIVERY_RETRY_SECS=2: attempts 12, succeeded 0, open 0, refused as not ready 12, may have typed 0". Run with BB_019_SPENT_WITHIN=600 (only to show today's behaviour), it fails at (2): T1's spent delivery is escalated to the supervisor and never re-issued (task 66). It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
